title: Does Overnight Return Predict the First Half-Hour Return for U.S. Market Indices?
one_line: Per an independent pre-registered NQ replication: the overnight return predicts the 09:30-10:00 return NEGATIVELY (β×100 = −4.15, t = −2.42, about half the paper's SPY strength), mostly in the first ~5 minutes, and it does not survive costs; trading with the overnight move fails; a narrowed version (buy NQ 09:35-10:00 after an extreme overnight drop that bounces at 09:35) was positive out of sample on 18 trades.

findings.statement: Replication on NQ: overnight return → first-half-hour return negative, β×100 = −4.15 (t = −2.42).
findings.evidence: NQ futures 2016-2026 (replicator's data); paper studies SPY/US indices.

findings.statement: Most of the reversal happens in the first ~5 minutes and does not survive costs.
Momentum (same direction as overnight) failed in every holding window.
Narrowed rule (overnight z ≤ −2 vs 60-day SD, 09:35 above 09:30 open, buy 09:35 → exit 10:00): out-of-sample 2022-2026 +50.9 pts/trade net, t = 2.49, 18 trades; train 2016-2021 +7.9 pts, t = 1.86.
findings.evidence: Pre-registered; 9 candidates chosen on training data.

why.pattern: Overnight overreaction corrected when full liquidity returns at the open.

tradable_edge: Supports overnight_reversal_first_hour_es; new spec nq_extreme_overnight_drop_rebound tests the narrowed version on our NQ/ES data.
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: The paper itself (SSRN 5807282) was not reachable; content comes from an independent replication on GitHub that cites it — treat paper-level numbers as unverified.
